nodes.name: ZIF-67 Solvothermal Synthesis
nodes.procedure: Cobalt nitrate hexahydrate (Co(NO₃)₂·6H₂O) and 2-methylimidazole (mIM) were dissolved in methanol at room temperature. The solution was then subjected to solvothermal treatment following the established method [22] to produce cubic ZIF-67 nanocubes with mean edge length of 158 nm.

unit_operations.name: Precursor Dissolution
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: Cobalt nitrate hexahydrate and 2-methylimidazole dissolved in methanol

nodes.source_text: As the platform material, cubic ZIF-67 is obtained following an established method[22] with a mean edge length of 158 nm (Figure 1B).

nodes.name: ZIF-67 Electrode Preparation
nodes.procedure: ZIF-67-modified carbon fiber paper (ZIF-67@CFP) electrode shows evenly coated ZIF-67 nanocubes on the carbon fiber surface.
nodes.source_text: The ZIF-67-modified carbon fiber paper (ZIF-67@CFP) electrode shows evenly coated ZIF-67 nanocubes on the carbon fiber surface (Figure 1C).

nodes.description: CV precatalytic treatment in 1.0 M KOH (0.1 V window: 0.925-1.025 V)
nodes.source_text: CV treatment in 1.0 M KOH electrolyte for 100 cycles using the ZIF-67@CFP electrode... After 40 cycles, the total anodic charge reaches 9.80 mC (1.02×10⁻⁴ mmol of Co²⁺), which is merely 1.3% of the total Co²⁺ (7.92×10⁻³ mmol) on the electrode.

nodes.description: CV precatalytic treatment in 1.0 M KOH (0.4 V window: 0.925-1.325 V)
nodes.source_text: At a wider potential window of 0.4... two recognizable redox couples... with half-wave potentials (E₁/₂) at 1.049 and 1.124 V... at the 40th cycle, anodic: 0.537 A g⁻¹; cathodic: 0.411 A g⁻¹.

nodes.description: CV precatalytic treatment in 1.0 M KOH (0.6 V window: 0.925-1.525 V)
nodes.source_text: A new anodic peak (peak potential Eₚ = 1.330 V, marked as region III) appears after cycling within 0.6... The 100th cycle shows a higher phase angle of 76° compared to 65°.

nodes.description: OER performance after CV precatalytic treatment (general)
nodes.source_text: The lowest overpotential for a current density of 1 A g⁻¹ is 205 mV after 15 cycles. The declining trend of turnover frequency (TOF) at an overpotential of 296 mV shows that the normalized activity of Co sites decreases from 0.59 s⁻¹ (after 3 cycles) to 0.06 s⁻¹ (after 100 cycles) with a 90% activity loss.

nodes.description: Amperometric pretreatment at 1.325 V followed by OER testing
nodes.source_text: OER overpotential at 10 A g⁻¹ decreases... to 300 mV (pretreated at 1.325 V)... the TOF (overpotential = 300 mV) maintains at ca. 0.24 s⁻¹... but drops to 0.13 and 0.043 s⁻¹ after pretreatment for 1500 and 3600 s... volcano-shaped overpotential trend... 239 mV (2500 s).

nodes.description: OER activity of CoOOH derived from α-Co(OH)₂
nodes.source_text: the CoOOH from α-Co(OH)₂ is most active (turnover frequency = 0.59 s⁻¹) compared to that from β-Co(OH)₂ (0.06 s⁻¹).

nodes.description: OER activity of CoOOH derived from β-Co(OH)₂
nodes.source_text: the CoOOH from α-Co(OH)₂ is most active (turnover frequency = 0.59 s⁻¹) compared to that from β-Co(OH)₂ (0.06 s⁻¹).

nodes.description: Amperometric OER performance comparison at different pretreatment potentials
nodes.source_text: the subsequent OER overpotential at 10 A g⁻¹ decreases from 341 mV (pretreated at 1.025 V) to 300 mV (pretreated at 1.325 V) with Tafel slope increasing from 78.6 to 99.4 mV dec⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cubic ZIF-67 nanocubes with mean edge length of 158 nm evenly coated on carbon fiber paper.
nodes.evidence_snippet: cubic ZIF-67 is obtained following an established method with a mean edge length of 158 nm (Figure 1B). The ZIF-67-modified carbon fiber paper (ZIF-67@CFP) electrode shows evenly coated ZIF-67 nanocubes on the carbon fiber surface (Figure 1C).

nodes.characterization_summary: Single ZIF-67 nanocube shows no clear crystalline structure; featureless SAED patterns rule out other Co-based structures; dark-field TEM with elemental mappings confirm uniform Co, N, O distribution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The transmission electron microscopy (TEM) image (Figure 1D) and the high-resolution images of selected regions (Figure 1E-G showing the center, corner, and edge regions) show no clear crystalline structure of ZIF-67, also indicated by the featureless selected area electron diffraction (SAED) patterns, such results rule out the other Co-based structures.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pristine ZIF-67 shows intensive peaks at 7.4° and 12.8° assigned to (011) and (112) facets; CV-treated samples show conversion to β-Co(OH)₂ (001) at 19.2° and CoOOH (003) at 19.7° depending on potential window.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 3A, the ex situ X-ray powder diffraction (XRD) pattern of pristine ZIF-67 matches well with the previous report, where two intensive peaks at 7.4 and 12.8° are assigned to (011) and (112) facets, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pristine ZIF-67 Co 2p₃/₂ peaks at 780.5, 782.1, 786.1 eV confirm Co²⁺; after CV treatment new Co³⁺ peak at 779.7 eV; N/Co ratio decreases from 3.63 to 0.21 indicating ZIF-67 destruction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The pristine ZIF-67 shows a surface N-to-Co atomic ratio of 3.63... the CV precatalytic treatments lead to the dramatic decrement of N-to-Co ratio to ... 0.21 (0.4 and 0.6) after 100 cycles.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ UV-vis shows tetrahedral Co sites in ZIF-67 with triplet peaks at 540, 566, 587 nm disappearing at 1.525 V; α-Co(OH)₂ peak at 620 nm persists until 1.465 V; Co³⁺ signal at 369 nm appears at 1.585 V.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 4C shows the UV–vis spectra of ZIF-67 at various applied potentials. At 0.925 V, in addition to the uprising absorption < 400 nm caused by the mIM linker, the broad absorption signal is obvious from 500 to 650 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows ZIF-67 peaks at 162, 179, 266, 687 cm⁻¹; α-Co(OH)₂ at 522, 629 cm⁻¹; β-Co(OH)₂ A₂ᵤ at 506 cm⁻¹; CoOOH A₁g at 571 cm⁻¹; confirms surface-limited conversion during first CV cycle.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The characteristic Raman peaks of ZIF-67 at 162 and 179 cm⁻¹ are attributed to the nitrogen-cobalt-nitrogen (N-Co-N) deformation vibration modes and the peaks at 266 and 687 cm⁻¹ to the C-CH₃ stretching of mIM linker molecules.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pristine ZIF-67 BET surface area is 932 m²/g with 1.7 nm pores; drops to 158 m²/g after 1h amperometry at 1.525 V; new pores 2.1-5.0 nm form after treatment.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 5H,I compares the pore size distribution and Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) surface area of pristine ZIF-67 and ZIF-67 samples treated by amperometry at different potentials for 1 h. The sub-2 nm pore observed from the pristine sample matches well with the theoretical 1.7 nm pore.

nodes.characterization_summary: After amperometry, deformed ZIF-67 shows polycrystalline structures; d-spacings of 1.59 Å (110), 2.13 Å (018) for α-Co(OH)₂; 2.25 Å (101) for β-Co(OH)₂; 2.43 Å (101) for CoOOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The d spacings of ca. 1.59 and 2.13 Å can be ascribed to the (110) and (018) planes of α-Co(OH)₂, respectively. The presence of β-Co(OH)₂ is also suggested by the d spacing of 2.25 Å, matching the (101) plane.
